quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #12
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: The most important thing to remember about speed and curves is that you must:

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter the curve, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Accelerate gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle's inertia makes it harder to turn in curves. You must slow down before entering a curve to stay in control.

questions.question: If you stop along the road at night, you should:

options.text: Turn off all your lights.
Use your parking lights only.
Use your headlights only.
Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beams on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beams on.
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers and leave your low beam headlights on. Other drivers must be able to clearly see your vehicle.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, you should:

options.text: Go to the next exit.
Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.
Flag down a police officer for an escort back to your exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the next exit.
questions.explanation: Take the next exit. Do not stop, back up, or cross the median. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: You should slow down:

options.text: On narrow or winding roads.
At intersections or railroad crossings.
When the road is wet or slippery.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You should slow down on narrow or winding roads, at intersections, at railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp or blind curves, where there are pedestrians or hazards, and when roads are wet or slippery.

questions.question: Emergency vehicles:

options.text: Have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and/or flashing lights.
May use a loudspeaker to give instructions.
May follow each other.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must yield to police cars, fire engines, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using sirens or horns and red or blue flashing lights. Follow any loudspeaker instructions. Emergency vehicles often follow each other, so only proceed when the way is clear.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only a blood alcohol level greater than the legal limit can
Alcohol does not
Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
Only a blood alcohol level greater than 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol reduces your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Your driving skills will suffer. No one can drink and drive safely.

questions.question: At an intersection with a stop sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for tailgating cars.
Move when the vehicle ahead of you moves.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first, since vehicles from the left are closer to you. Then look right, then look left again to check for vehicles you may have missed.

questions.question: When driving up a hill and approaching a heavy truck from behind, you should know that:

options.text: The truck may travel slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles often travel slower than the speed limit, especially on hills. Be careful when approaching from behind. Passing is illegal on hills with limited visibility.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, you should:

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed without braking and carefully turn back onto the pavement. Watch for nearby traffic when re-entering the road.

questions.question: When driving near heavy trucks, you must account for:

options.text: The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.
The decreased stopping distance required by large vehicles.
The decreased noise of larger vehicles.
The increased speed of larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more distance to stop. Stay in areas where the truck driver can see you and where your view of traffic is not blocked.

questions.question: When two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
One driver may continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: The driver on the right has the right-of-way. You must yield to them. You can proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn ahead. Slow down.
Work crew ahead.
Side road.
Playground ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sharp turn ahead. Slow down.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you a sharp turn is coming. Reduce your speed.

questions.question: What does a green arrow on a lane control signal mean?

options.text: You may use this lane.
No traffic is allowed in this lane.
You have the right-of-way.
You must merge into this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may use this lane.
questions.explanation: A steady green arrow pointing down means you can use that lane.

questions.question: How should you safely pass a bicycle?

options.text: Honk to let the bicyclist know you're passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Speed up and pass quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and give bicyclists plenty of space. They have less protection than car drivers. Passing too fast or too close can cause them to lose control.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Slam on the brakes.
Hold the steering wheel tight and slow to a stop.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on flashers and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tight and slow to a stop.
questions.explanation: Grip the wheel firmly and stay in your lane. Let off the gas slowly. Once you are going very slowly, brake lightly and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: You are angry from something that happened at work. When you reach your car, what should you do?

options.text: Play the radio loudly to distract yourself.
Drive fast on the highway to let off steam.
Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
Stop for drinks before driving home.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
questions.explanation: Wait and cool off before driving. Driving while angry is dangerous for you and others on the road.

questions.question: You are waiting at a stop sign behind other vehicles. After they pass and there is no cross traffic, you should:

options.text: Proceed through without stopping again.
Stop again at the stop sign before proceeding.
Slowly roll past the stop sign.
Follow the vehicle ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop again at the stop sign before proceeding.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop at every stop sign. Check for traffic before proceeding.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?

options.text: You may pass, even if dangerous.
Traffic moves in opposite directions.
You may not pass.
You may pass if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A dashed white line means lanes go the same direction. You can cross it to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Don't drink if you will drive.
Slippery when wet.
Road curves ahead.
A hill is coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when it is wet.

questions.question: How should you prepare for hazards ahead on the road?

options.text: Look at the entire road and all sides.
Stare straight ahead.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake.
Focus on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and all sides.
questions.explanation: Scan the entire road, including the sides. Look far ahead to spot problems early. This helps you handle dangerous situations safely.

questions.question: Can you drive around the gates at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Yes, when the train has passed.
No, never.
Yes, when the lights stop flashing.
Yes, if other drivers do it.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: You must stop at all railroad crossings when you see warning signals. These signals include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a person signaling, or train horns. Never try to go around a lowered gate.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: It is safe for other drivers to follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle with two people is more balanced than one with just the rider.
You must move completely into the left lane before passing a motorcycle.
You can expect a motorcycle's brake lights to come on when the rider slows down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must move completely into the left lane before passing a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use a full lane. Move your entire vehicle into the left lane before passing a motorcycle.

questions.question: What should you NOT do when changing lanes?

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Use your turn signal.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call police to check if the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call police to check if the road is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal to tell other drivers. Look for other drivers who may also be changing into your lane. Do not use your phone while driving.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Stop where you are.
Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights behind you, slow down and safely move to the right side of the road. Stop to let the emergency vehicle pass. If you are in heavy traffic, move slowly until you can get out of the way.

questions.question: You turn left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. Where should your car be after the turn?

options.text: In the right lane.
In the center of the street.
In the left lane.
In the lane with the least traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left lane.
questions.explanation: When turning left onto a one-way street, finish your turn in the left lane. This lane is closest to the lane you just left.

questions.question: When you turn, you should ____ your speed.

options.text: Increase
Keep the same
Change constantly
Decrease

questions.correctAnswerText: Decrease
questions.explanation: Slow down when turning. This helps you control your vehicle, stay in your lane, and handle unexpected situations.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow traffic light?

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep driving—you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
See what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a red light is coming. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: Which of these helps direct drivers into the correct lanes on highways?

options.text: Flashing red lights
Flashing yellow lights
White lines on the side of the road
White arrows in the middle of lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of lanes
questions.explanation: White arrows mark which lanes to use for driving straight or turning.

questions.question: You are in the right lane of a highway and want to move to the left lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check your side mirror and turn on your signal.
Do all of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for traffic. Always use your turn signal when changing lanes.

questions.question: What does a yellow and black diamond-shaped sign mean?

options.text: It warns you about road or traffic conditions ahead.
It helps you find cities and towns.
It tells you about traffic laws.
It tells you about road construction.

questions.correctAnswerText: It warns you about road or traffic conditions ahead.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs with black symbols or words on a yellow background are warning signs. They tell you about conditions on or near the road ahead.

questions.question: When can you carefully continue through an intersection on a yellow light?

options.text: An emergency vehicle is crossing your lane.
Pedestrians are crossing.
You are turning right.
You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow.
questions.explanation: If the light turns yellow while you are already in the intersection, you should continue through carefully.

questions.question: What factors affect how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach
Your body weight
How much time passes between drinks
All three of these

questions.correctAnswerText: All three of these
questions.explanation: Alcohol's effects depend on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your body weight. Eating food can slow alcohol absorption, but it cannot prevent impairment if you drink too much.

questions.question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?

options.text: Only behind your vehicle
Only on the left and right sides
Only in front of your vehicle
On all sides of your vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of your vehicle
questions.explanation: Keep space around all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to hazards. Do not crowd vehicles on your left and right sides.

questions.question: When can you cross a solid yellow line?

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction
During daylight hours only
At any time
When you are making a turn

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are making a turn
questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed, but solid lines cannot. You may cross a solid yellow line only when turning.

questions.question: How can you tell if you are stopped at a safe distance behind another vehicle?

options.text: You can read its license plate
You can see the ground under the vehicle's rear wheels
You can read its bumper stickers
You can count the passengers in the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see the ground under the vehicle's rear wheels
questions.explanation: When stopped behind another vehicle, stay back far enough to see the ground under its rear wheels. This gives you space to move around the vehicle if needed and protects you if the vehicle rolls backward.

questions.question: What must you do when making a right turn on a green light?

options.text: Keep your normal driving speed
Stop and look for police cars
Yield to pedestrians
Speed up

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians
questions.explanation: You may turn right or left on a green light unless a sign says otherwise. When turning, you must yield to other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection.

questions.question: What greatly increases stopping distance and crash severity?

options.text: High speeds
Slow speeds
Driving at night
Driving uphill

questions.correctAnswerText: High speeds
questions.explanation: High speeds greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity. The faster you drive, the harder the impact if you crash.

questions.question: What is a 'No zone'?

options.text: Blind spots around a truck or bus
A special speed zone
A roadway with restrictions on stereo volume
A television show that replaced The Twilight Zone

questions.correctAnswerText: Blind spots around a truck or bus
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on both sides, in the rear, and in the front. Cars cannot be seen in these areas. These blind spots are called the 'No zone.'

questions.question: You are waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection, but opposing traffic blocks your view. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up as soon as the first lane clears
Wait until you can see all lanes you need to cross before turning
Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across
Move into each lane of traffic as it clears

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all lanes you need to cross before turning
questions.explanation: Never start a left turn until you can see that all lanes you need to cross are clear and you can turn safely.

questions.question: When driving across a railroad track with no signals or gates, what should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains
You can pass slower drivers while crossing
Make sure your vehicle can completely cross the tracks without stopping
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can completely cross the tracks without stopping
questions.explanation: Before driving onto railroad tracks, make sure you have enough space to cross completely without stopping. Never pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing. Always check for trains before crossing tracks.
